vocabulary.term: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
vocabulary.termEs: Números racionales en la recta numérica
vocabulary.definition: Every rational number has one exact spot on the number line. Writing it as a fraction, a decimal, or an integer does not change where it sits.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cada número racional tiene un lugar exacto en la recta numérica. Escribirlo como fracción, decimal o entero no cambia dónde queda.
vocabulary.visual: −3/2 = −1.5 and 1/2 = 0.5 each sit at one exact point.
vocabulary.cloze: A rational number always has one exact spot on the ___ ___.

examples.why: Its value decides where it goes, not its form.
The digits are not the value — -3/4 is less than one unit from 0.

vocabulary.definition: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers, with a bottom number that is not zero.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que se puede escribir como una fracción de dos enteros, con un denominador que no sea cero.
vocabulary.visual: −1/2, 0 and 5/4 each sit at one exact point.
vocabulary.cloze: A number you can write as a fraction of two integers, with a bottom number that is not zero, is a ___.

examples.why: It can be written as −3/1 — both parts are integers.
It can be written as 3/4, so it is rational.

vocabulary.definition: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que muestra una parte de un todo, como 3/4.
vocabulary.visual: 3/4 means 3 out of 4 equal parts — like 3 slices of a pizza cut into 4
vocabulary.cloze: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/5, is a ___.

examples.text: -3/4 as a point three-quarters of the way from 0 to -1
examples.why: It names a part of a whole and has a place on the line.
Two separate digits are not a part of a whole.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.visual: 0.5 = 1/2 (halfway between 0 and 1 on the number line)
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show parts of a whole is a ___.

examples.why: The decimal part places it between two integers.
Dropping the point changes the value entirely.

vocabulary.definition: A straight line where numbers are placed in order; numbers get smaller to the left and larger to the right.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una recta donde los números se colocan en orden; los números son menores a la izquierda y mayores a la derecha.

examples.text: A line with -3, 0 and 3 marked in order

copyPanel.rule: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
steps: 1. Find the two consecutive integers the rational number falls between
2. Divide the segment between integers into equal parts matching the denominator
3. Negative numbers move to the left of zero; positive numbers move to the right

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Andrew's Reasoning about Opposites
revealWordProblem.text:
Andrew made the generalization about opposite numbers shown on the note: if x and y are both greater than 0 and x < y, then −x > −y.
Question: Do you agree with Andrew's statement? Explain your reasoning using a number line.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A sticky note reading: If x and y are both greater than 0 and x is less than y, then negative x is greater than negative y.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: I agree. Try numbers first: let x = 2 and y = 5, so x < y is true. Their opposites are −2 and −5, and on a number line −2 sits to the right of −5, so −2 > −5, which is exactly what Andrew claims. This works every time: taking the opposite reflects each number across 0, so the number that was closer to 0 on the right is still closer to 0 on the left — and on a number line the number farther right is greater. So the smaller positive always has the greater opposite.

questions.stem: Which point is located between -1 and -2 on the number line?
questions.explanation: -1.5 is between -1 and -2 because it is 0.5 units to the left of -1 (or 0.5 units to the right of -2).
choiceFeedback: This value is farther left than -2, so it lands between -2 and -3. Look for a number just past -1 heading toward -2.
-0.5 sits between 0 and -1 — it has not traveled past -1 yet. You need a number that lands beyond -1 but before -2.
That value is positive, which puts it on the right side of 0. Both -1 and -2 sit to the left of 0, so the number you need is negative.
hints: 'Between -1 and -2' is on the NEGATIVE side, in the gap from -1 to -2.
Turn each choice into a spot on the number line and check: is it past -1 but not past -2?
Start at -1 and move half a unit farther left. Which choice lands in that gap between -1 and -2?
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué punto está ubicado entre -1 y -2 en la recta numérica?
questions.explanationEs: -1.5 está entre -1 y -2 porque queda 0.5 unidades a la izquierda de -1 (o 0.5 unidades a la derecha de -2).
hintsEs: 'Entre −1 y −2' está del lado NEGATIVO, en el espacio de −1 a −2.
Convierte cada opción en un punto de la recta numérica y revisa: ¿pasa de −1 pero no pasa de −2?
Empieza en −1 y muévete media unidad más a la izquierda. ¿Qué opción cae en ese espacio entre −1 y −2?

choiceFeedback: This fraction is about 0.333, so it is bigger than 0.25. Convert the decimal into hundredths and reduce that fraction.
This fraction equals 0.4 as a decimal, which is larger than 0.25. Write 0.25 as a fraction over 100 first, then simplify.
hints: Read 0.25 as a place-value number: 25 hundredths.
Write it as 25/100, then simplify by dividing the top and bottom by the same number.
Divide both 25 and 100 by 25. What simpler fraction do you get?
hintsEs: Lee 0.25 como un número con valor posicional: 25 centésimas.
Escríbelo como 25/100 y luego simplifica dividiendo arriba y abajo entre el mismo número.
Divide 25 y 100 entre 25. ¿Qué fracción más simple obtienes?

questions.stem: Where is -3/4 located on the number line?
questions.explanation: -3/4 = -0.75, which is between 0 and -1. It is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. -3/4 = -0.75, which is between ___ and ___.
-3/4 is less than one whole unit away from 0, so it never even reaches -1. Convert the fraction to a decimal and see how far left it travels.
The distance is right, but the negative sign puts this number to the left of 0, not to the right.
hints: The size of -3/4 is less than 1 whole — its distance from zero is under 1.
Convert: 3/4 = 0.75, so -3/4 = -0.75. Now ask which two numbers -0.75 sits between on the line.
Start at 0 and move 0.75 units LEFT. Did you pass -1 on the way, or not?
questions.stemEs: ¿Dónde se ubica -3/4 en la recta numérica?
questions.explanationEs: -3/4 = -0.75, que está entre 0 y -1. Queda a 3/4 del camino de 0 hacia -1.
hintsEs: El tamaño de −3/4 es menor que 1 entero: su distancia desde cero es menor que 1.
Convierte: 3/4 = 0.75, así que −3/4 = −0.75. Ahora pregunta entre qué dos números queda −0.75 en la recta.
Empieza en 0 y muévete 0.75 unidades a la IZQUIERDA. ¿Pasaste el −1 en el camino o no?

reviewHighlights.rule: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
steps: 1. Find the two consecutive integers the rational number falls between
2. Divide the segment between integers into equal parts matching the denominator
3. Negative numbers move to the left of zero; positive numbers move to the right
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Rational Numbers on the Number Line is treating the numerator and denominator of a negative fraction as two separate integers instead of one value between two integers — for example, plotting -3/4 by going to -3 and then counting 4 more units to the left, landing (incorrectly) at -7, instead of recognizing that -3/4 = -0.75, which sits between 0 and -1. Before you submit an answer, find the two integers your value falls between, then split that space into equal parts.

level1.stem: A point is halfway between −9 and −8. What number is it?
level1.stemEs: Un punto está a la mitad entre −9 y −8. ¿Qué número es?
hints: Halfway between 8 and 9 is 8.5. This point is left of 0.
hintsEs: La mitad entre 8 y 9 es 8.5. Este punto está a la izquierda del 0.
level1.explanation: Find halfway between 8 and 9: 8 + 0.5 = 8.5 Use a − sign: −8.5
level1.explanationEs: Halla la mitad entre 8 y 9: 8 + 0.5 = 8.5 Usa el signo −: −8.5

level1.stem: The space from 0 to −1 has 4 equal parts. What number is 1 part to the left of 0?
level1.stemEs: El espacio de 0 a −1 tiene 4 partes iguales. ¿Qué número está 1 parte a la izquierda del 0?
hints: Each part is 1/4. Left of 0 is negative.
hintsEs: Cada parte es 1/4. A la izquierda del 0 es negativo.
level1.explanation: Find one part: 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25 Go 1 part left of 0: −0.25
level1.explanationEs: Halla una parte: 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25 Ve 1 parte a la izquierda del 0: −0.25

level1.stem: Which integer is just to the left of −0.5 on a number line?
level1.stemEs: ¿Qué entero está justo a la izquierda de −0.5 en una recta numérica?
hints: −0.5 is between two integers. Pick the one farther from 0.
hintsEs: −0.5 está entre dos enteros. Escoge el que está más lejos del 0.
level1.explanation: Find the two integers: −1 and 0 Pick the one on the left: −1
level1.explanationEs: Halla los dos enteros: −1 y 0 Escoge el de la izquierda: −1

level1.stem: A point is halfway between 2 and 3. What number is it?
level1.stemEs: Un punto está a la mitad entre 2 y 3. ¿Qué número es?
hints: Halfway means one half of a unit past 2.
hintsEs: A la mitad significa medio entero después del 2.
level1.explanation: Find the two integers: 2 and 3 Add one half to 2: 2 + 0.5 = 2.5
level1.explanationEs: Halla los dos enteros: 2 y 3 Suma un medio a 2: 2 + 0.5 = 2.5

level1.stem: Point A is on the number line. What number is at point A? Write a decimal.
level1.stemEs: El punto A está en la recta numérica. ¿Qué número está en el punto A? Escribe un decimal.
hints: Start at −3. Count the small spaces to point A. Each space is 0.25.
hintsEs: Empieza en −3. Cuenta los espacios pequeños hasta el punto A. Cada espacio es 0.25.
level1.explanation: Find the integers around A: −4 and −3 Count spaces left from −3: 1 space = 0.25 Name the point: A = −3.25
level1.explanationEs: Halla los enteros alrededor de A: −4 y −3 Cuenta espacios a la izquierda desde −3: 1 espacio = 0.25 Nombra el punto: A = −3.25

buildFigure.caption: Each space is one fourth of a unit.
buildFigure.captionEs: Cada espacio es un cuarto de unidad.

level2.stem: Ray says −4.5 goes halfway between −4 and −3. Is he right? Where does −4.5 go?
level2.stemEs: Ray dice que −4.5 va a la mitad entre −4 y −3. ¿Tiene razón? ¿Dónde va −4.5?
hints: Is −4.5 more than 4 units from 0, or less?
hintsEs: ¿−4.5 está a más de 4 unidades del 0, o a menos?
level2.explanation: Find how far −4.5 is from 0: 4.5 units left of 0 Find the two integers around it: −5 and −4
level2.explanationEs: Halla qué tan lejos está −4.5 del 0: 4.5 unidades a la izquierda del 0 Halla los dos enteros a su alrededor: −5 y −4
choiceFeedback: That is Ray's mistake. −3.5 goes there. −4.5 is farther from 0 than −4.
4.5 is positive. −4.5 is to the left of 0.
The .5 is one half, not a digit 5.

level2.stem: What number is 3 of 10 equal parts from 0 toward −1? Write a decimal.
level2.stemEs: ¿Qué número está a 3 de 10 partes iguales desde 0 hacia −1? Escribe un decimal.
hints: Each part is 0.1. Count to the left of 0.
hintsEs: Cada parte es 0.1. Cuenta a la izquierda del 0.
level2.explanation: Find the size of one part: 1 ÷ 10 = 0.1 Count 3 parts left of 0: 3 × 0.1 = 0.3 → −0.3
level2.explanationEs: Halla el tamaño de una parte: 1 ÷ 10 = 0.1 Cuenta 3 partes a la izquierda del 0: 3 × 0.1 = 0.3 → −0.3

level2.stem: A point is halfway between −6 and −5. What number is it?
level2.stemEs: Un punto está a la mitad entre −6 y −5. ¿Qué número es?
hints: Halfway between 5 and 6 is 5.5. This point is left of 0.
hintsEs: La mitad entre 5 y 6 es 5.5. Este punto está a la izquierda del 0.
level2.explanation: Find halfway between 5 and 6: 5 + 0.5 = 5.5 Use a − sign. It is left of 0: −5.5
level2.explanationEs: Halla la mitad entre 5 y 6: 5 + 0.5 = 5.5 Usa el signo −. Está a la izquierda del 0: −5.5

level2.stem: Point K is between −4 and −3. It is 0.4 units from −4. What number is K?
level2.stemEs: El punto K está entre −4 y −3. Está a 0.4 unidades de −4. ¿Qué número es K?
hints: Start at −4. To stay between −4 and −3, which way must you move?
hintsEs: Empieza en −4. Para quedarte entre −4 y −3, ¿hacia dónde debes moverte?
level2.explanation: Start at −4: −4 Move 0.4 to the right, toward −3: −4 + 0.4 = −3.6
level2.explanationEs: Empieza en −4: −4 Muévete 0.4 a la derecha, hacia −3: −4 + 0.4 = −3.6

level2.stem: The water in a pool is 1 1/4 feet under the top edge. The top edge is 0. Write the water level as a decimal.
level2.stemEs: El agua de una piscina está 1 1/4 pies bajo el borde de arriba. El borde de arriba es 0. Escribe el nivel del agua como un decimal.
hints: Under the edge means less than 0. 1/4 = 0.25.
hintsEs: Bajo el borde significa menos que 0. 1/4 = 0.25.
level2.explanation: Write 1/4 as a decimal: 1/4 = 0.25 Make it negative. It is under the edge: 1 1/4 = 1.25 → −1.25
level2.explanationEs: Escribe 1/4 como decimal: 1/4 = 0.25 Hazlo negativo. Está bajo el borde: 1 1/4 = 1.25 → −1.25

level3.stem: Between which two consecutive integers does −3.5 fall on a number line?
choiceFeedback: Both of those sit to the RIGHT of negative 3.5. Half a unit below negative 3 lands to its left.
Those are positive. This number is negative, so it sits left of zero.
Both of those sit to the LEFT of negative 3.5.
level3.explanation: −3.5 is half a unit to the left of −3, which places it between −4 and −3.

level3.stem: Lia plots −1 1/3. She splits −1 to −2 into 3 parts. Then she counts 1 part to the right of −1. What number did she really plot?
level3.stemEs: Lia marca −1 1/3. Divide de −1 a −2 en 3 partes. Luego cuenta 1 parte a la derecha de −1. ¿Qué número marcó en realidad?
hints: 1 part to the right of −1 moves toward 0. Each part is 1/3.
hintsEs: 1 parte a la derecha de −1 se mueve hacia el 0. Cada parte es 1/3.
level3.explanation: Start at −1 and move right: −1 + 1/3 Name the point she plotted: −3/3 + 1/3 = −2/3
level3.explanationEs: Empieza en −1 y muévete a la derecha: −1 + 1/3 Nombra el punto que marcó: −3/3 + 1/3 = −2/3

level3.stem: Point R is between −6 and −5. It is 0.3 units from −5. What number is R?
level3.stemEs: El punto R está entre −6 y −5. Está a 0.3 unidades de −5. ¿Qué número es R?
hints: Start at −5. Move toward −6.
hintsEs: Empieza en −5. Muévete hacia −6.
level3.explanation: Start at −5: −5 Move 0.3 to the left, toward −6: −5 − 0.3 = −5.3
level3.explanationEs: Empieza en −5: −5 Muévete 0.3 a la izquierda, hacia −6: −5 − 0.3 = −5.3

level3.stem: A freezer's temperature is between −10°F and −9°F. It is 3/4 of the way from −9°F to −10°F. Write the temperature as a decimal.
level3.stemEs: La temperatura de un congelador está entre −10 °F y −9 °F. Está a 3/4 del camino de −9 °F a −10 °F. Escribe la temperatura como un decimal.
hints: Start at −9. Move 3/4 of a unit toward −10.
hintsEs: Empieza en −9. Muévete 3/4 de unidad hacia −10.
level3.explanation: Write 3/4 as a decimal: 3/4 = 0.75 Move 0.75 left from −9: −9 − 0.75 = −9.75
level3.explanationEs: Escribe 3/4 como decimal: 3/4 = 0.75 Muévete 0.75 a la izquierda desde −9: −9 − 0.75 = −9.75

level3.stem: Find the number exactly halfway between −1 1/2 and −1/4 on a number line.
level3.stemEs: Halla el número que está exactamente a la mitad entre −1 1/2 y −1/4 en una recta numérica.
hints: Write both as decimals. Find the distance between them, then go half of it.
hintsEs: Escribe los dos como decimales. Halla la distancia entre ellos y luego avanza la mitad.
level3.explanation: Write both as decimals: −1.5 and −0.25 Find the distance between them: 1.5 − 0.25 = 1.25 Go half the distance from −1.5: 1.25 ÷ 2 = 0.625; −1.5 + 0.625 = −0.875
level3.explanationEs: Escribe los dos como decimales: −1.5 y −0.25 Halla la distancia entre ellos: 1.5 − 0.25 = 1.25 Avanza la mitad de la distancia desde −1.5: 1.25 ÷ 2 = 0.625; −1.5 + 0.625 = −0.875

tool.title: Place the Rational Numbers
tool.caption: Every tick is one half. Drag each number to its exact spot before you answer the problems below.

steps.title: Try numbers
steps.say: Pick two positives with x less than y.

steps.title: Find the opposites
steps.math: opposite of 2 is −2; opposite of 5 is −5

steps.title: Compare on the number line
steps.say: Farther right on the line means greater.

steps.title: Explain why it always works
steps.say: The smaller positive always has the greater opposite.

workedSteps.answer: Yes, I agree: if 0 < x < y, then −x > −y (for example, 2 < 5 and −2 > −5).
